messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  

This is derived from the water phase diagram: as pressure falls below atmospheric, the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward, so the temperature at which ice melts (or water freezes) becomes lower. At 10 kPa the equilibrium lies near –2 °C, slightly below the 0 °C freezing point at 101.3 kPa.
